**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding** – no standardised first-touch experience; unclear how new members move from sign-up → first class → retention checkpoint
- **Churn & pause management** – no documented trigger points, re-engagement sequences, or pause-to-cancel pathways; losing money by not acting early
- **Coaching standards audit** – Class Quality Audit Checklist exists nowhere; coaches have no feedback loop on consistency, form correction, cueing
- **Retention win-back** – no systematic approach to lapsed members; ad-hoc outreach only
- **Member data & GDPR** – no documented handling of sign-ups, payment info, communications consent, deletion requests; compliance risk
- **Incident & complaints** – no formal escalation, resolution, or safeguarding log (especially critical in women-only space)
- **Health & safety inductions** – no SOP for onboarding members to gym safety, equipment, emergency procedures
- **Finance/billing disputes** – no SOP for refunds, chargebacks, frozen accounts, payment failures
- **Milestone recognition** – no process to celebrate member wins (first class, attendance streaks, goal hits); lost retention lever

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your coaches' needs FIRST (counterintuitive, but critical)**
Have each coach list every variation they currently sell or could sell—classes, PT rates, packages, add-ons. You'll find inconsistency (your selling point). Now standardise: pick 3-4 tiers (e.g., "Foundation," "Accelerator," "Transform") with fixed pricing. Coaches get a one-page laminate card they memorise by Friday. This stops members hearing different prices and coaches underselling.

**2. Create TWO separate visual menus (not one confusing sheet)**
Members see: class schedule + monthly membership tiers + PT pricing + bolt-ons (nutrition consult, progress tracking). Coaches see: commission structure per tier + upsell triggers (when to pitch PT to group class members). Post the member version by the desk; laminate the coach version.

**3. Define "what's included" obsessively—this is your conversion engine**
Don't just list "unlimited classes." Write: "Access to 18+ weekly classes + form checks in every session + quarterly fitness assessment." Members need to feel the value before pricing. Coaches need to know what they're delivering so they stop giving extras away for free.

**4. Price psychology tweak: anchor aggressively**
Show your premium tier *first* in any communication. Make mid-tier look like the "smart choice." Most women will default to middle option. This is standard but works—especially in fitness.

You need July's volume back *at* August's cost, not a trade-off between them.

- **Audit your pricing tiers now.** October's 174 members should yield ~£22k+ revenue at July's £145/member rate; you're £4.5k short. Review: are new joiners on intro rates not graduating? Are class packs underselling monthly memberships? Move discount joiners to 6-week upgrade deadline or lose them.
- **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May** (post-move) but stabilised at 3–6% since. **Target: get to 2–3% by November** via retention email sequence (60-day engagement check-in) and early-churn intervention for members who've not booked a class in 10 days.

- **Quiet class fill:** Identify your lowest-attendance slot (likely early morning or mid-week afternoon). Offer £5 "bring a friend free" vouchers or bundle 10-class packs at £99 (vs £120 à la carte) to drive volume.

- **Pull full P&L for Sep–Oct immediately.** You have cash movement data (Starling), not cost data. Find: are staff hours up? Rent higher in new space? Utilities spiked? If payroll or rent now exceed 50% of revenue, you've over-invested in the studio footprint and must either (a) fill it faster or (b) cut back-office hours.
